what_worked: Decision-oriented framing with actionable takeaways per slide creates a genuinely useful narrative arc.
fix_next: Multiple fabricated numbers ($133.8M revenue, $4.3K AI median, $350 Productivity median, 12-month framing) undermine credibility; verify every stat against the actual dataset.
verdict: Strong narrative structure badly undermined by numerous fabricated or inflated figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: '$133.8M combined 12-month revenue' — dataset shows $15.6M 30-day revenue; no 12-month field exists, and 8.6x extrapolation is unjustified. Slide 2: AI median stated as '$4.3K' — reference is $503. Productivity median stated as '$350' — reference is $79.91. Marketing/Education '3-4x the median revenue of AI' is wrong given actual medians ($2,370/$2,435 vs $503 ≈ 4.7-4.8x, but their own $4.3K base makes the ratio ~0.6x). Chart y-axis shows values up to $16K for median which doesn't match any category. Slide 4: Stripe share stated as 64-65% — reference is 636/936≈67.9% (minor). Slide 5: MRR table presents fabricated monthly figures (e.g., Education $2,142, AI $446) that don't match dataset medians even after dividing by 12. Title promises 'Five decisions' but only four are delivered (slides 2-5).

evidence.insight: The revenue-per-entrant framing (slide 2) and median-vs-mean acquisition multiple distinction (slide 3) show genuine analytical thinking beyond chart description. The follower-count dismissal (slide 4) is a useful contrarian finding.
evidence.narrative: Clear decision-briefing structure with numbered decisions, each slide ending with an actionable recommendation banner. Coherent thesis of 'where to build, what to pay, what to ignore.' Missing the promised 5th decision.
evidence.framing: Audience (indie/micro-SaaS builders and acquirers) is clearly stated on slide 1. However, no mention of missing data (274 missing categories, 288 missing audience_type, 241 missing country), no limitations section, and the 12-month revenue framing is unsubstantiated.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 1 inflates total revenue ~8.6x without justification. Slide 2 AI median off by ~8.5x ($4.3K vs $503), Productivity median off by ~4.4x ($350 vs $79.91). Slide 5 MRR table values don't correspond to dataset medians divided by 12 (Education: $2,435/12=$203 not $2,142). The deck systematically presents fabricated or miscalculated figures.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark-navy/orange color scheme, clean chart types (dual-axis bar+line, horizontal bar, donut, table), good use of callout boxes. Legible typography and clear hierarchy. Chart on slide 2 has readable axes. Donut chart on slide 4 is clean.
evidence.ai_slop: Minor consulting-style language ('decision briefing,' 'sharp wedge') but generally restrained. The systematic fabrication of plausible-looking but wrong numbers is more concerning than typical AI slop.
